findings.title: Capture native ownership before readiness and bound migration/startup/disposal
findings.trigger: Migration hangs, Miniflare.ready rejects/hangs after constructing native instance, or dispose never resolves.
findings.why: worker is assigned only after unchanged startMiniflare finishes synchronous migration and mf.ready. Failure before return leaves no handle/PIDs available to finally; the driver then removes the owned state when !worker even though an orphan may still use it. Neither startup/dispose nor socket listening has a driver-owned terminal deadline. The shared helper confirms this boundary, so no new backend reproduction is claimed.
findings.requiredFix: Use separately reviewed new owned launcher/supervisor with bounded migration and ready/dispose deadlines; capture exact native handle/process ownership before ready, dispose only owned resources on failed start, preserve failed native state/evidence until disposal is confirmed. Do not edit original helper or kill by process name.

findings.title: Bound fixture setup transport through body consumption
findings.trigger: Any workspace/invite/join/assignment setup fetch or response body stalls.
findings.why: The setup client is the unchanged shared client, whose fetch and response.text have no timeout. Direct case raw at73 uses AbortSignal.timeout20000 correctly through74, but that bound does not cover setup; a hang prevents terminal reporting and runtime disposal.
findings.requiredFix: Use a new locally owned bounded transport for every setup request and body read, retaining actual status/headers/body or partial failure, no retries/substituted status. Add lightweight header/body-stall controls before reviewed native execution.

findings.title: Checkpoint per-case raw custody before a timeout can abort the scenario
findings.trigger: HTTP headers arrive and the body aborts, transport throws, or post-response D1 snapshot fails.
findings.why: The before snapshot and response are local until both raw and after complete. Observation is appended only afterward, so catch retains only an error stack, losing that case before-state and partial response/status; finally can then delete failed D1 state. This falls short of the prepared contract raw-failure custody.
findings.requiredFix: Append/checkpoint a running case with before-state before dispatch, preserve headers and each partial body receipt before parsing/assertions, attach failure and best-available after/final native custody in bounded finally, and retain failed state. Count completed cases only when the declared case reaches a truthful terminal result.
